title: Soil
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 3 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child lists the characteristics of sand, clay and loam and names ways of conserving soil (mulching, manuring, planting trees).

floor.question: Which soil makes a long ribbon when rolled wet?

representations: samples of sand, clay and loam
bottles with holes for a drainage test
a mulched tray and a bare tray
steps: Feel each soil and say how it feels.
Say which is best for plants.
Name ways to care for soil.
contexts: a river bank washed away by rain

board.do: Draw three heaps: sand, clay, loam.

board.say: How does this feel when wet?

board.do: Wait for the child to say smooth and sticky.
Write a word under each: rough, sticky, crumbly.

misconceptions.ask: Is sand the same as clay soil?
misconceptions.repair: Let the child rub sand and clay between the fingers and roll each wet. Name the feel.

misconceptions.ask: Water is poured on sand and on clay. Which lets water through faster?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water through sand and clay in two bottles with holes. Count how fast it drips.

misconceptions.ask: Which soil is best for growing vegetables?
misconceptions.repair: Grow beans in sand, clay and loam pots. Watch which grows best. Name loam.

misconceptions.ask: Which garden protects the soil better: bare soil or soil covered with dry grass?
misconceptions.repair: Pour water on a bare tray and a mulched tray of soil. See which washes away.

checks.question: Name one way to conserve soil.
